sources.name: Gemini Apps Help: Get personalization with memory of your past Gemini chats

caption:
Gemini now has a page that shows what it remembers about you, from your city to your job.
It lives in Settings, then Personal Intelligence, then Memory summary, and you can fix or delete any of it in plain words.
Here is how to find it and clean it up.

Would you check what your AI knows about you?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: 9to5Google · Photo: 9to5Google
threads_text: Gemini now shows you a Memory summary: everything it has learned about you from past chats, sorted into sections you can edit or delete. It sits under Settings, then Personal Intelligence. Have you ever checked what your AI assistant remembers about you?

slides.headline: How to see *what Gemini remembers* about you, and delete it

slides.heading: 1. Settings, then *Personal Intelligence*
paras: On gemini.google.com, open Settings, then Personal Intelligence, then the Memory summary tab.
It needs Memory and Keep activity turned on.

slides.heading: 2. Read *The Essentials*
paras: Your memory is split into sections: The Essentials, career, travel, media and fitness.
The Essentials holds your background, location and key relationships.

slides.heading: 3. Fix it in *plain words*
paras: Type what to add or remove in the box at the bottom. The pencil icon allows bigger edits.

paras.t: Memory history shows when each detail was added.

slides.heading: 4. Delete the *source chats* too
paras: To make Gemini forget something for good, Google says to delete the chats that contain it.
Memory is not used in Gems or Live chats.

site_article.headline: How to see what Gemini remembers about you with Memory summary
site_article.dek: Gemini now collects what it has learned from your chats into one page. Here is where to find it, who can use it, and how to edit or delete what is there.
site_article.summary: Gemini's Memory summary shows what the assistant has learned about you from past chats, sorted into sections you can edit or delete. On the web it sits under Settings, then Personal Intelligence, and it needs Memory and Keep activity turned on.
site_article.seo_title: How to see what Gemini remembers about you (Memory summary)
site_article.seo_description: Find Gemini's Memory summary, see what it knows about you, edit it in plain words, check Memory history, and delete what it should forget.
site_article.answer_summary: Open gemini.google.com, go to Settings, then Personal Intelligence, then the Memory summary tab. Memory and Keep activity must be on, and Google limits the feature to US users with a Google AI plan for now.
site_article.hero_alt: The Gemini desktop app open on a Windows computer screen.

paragraphs.text: Gemini now shows you what it remembers about you. The feature is called Memory summary, and it collects what Gemini has picked up from your past chats into one page you can read, correct and delete. 9to5Google reported the rollout on November 9, 2026, and Google describes it as a way to view, edit and delete what Gemini Apps understands about you.

Two things have to be true before it shows up. Memory itself must be on, and Keep activity must be on, because Google's help page says the memory feature is not available when Keep activity is off. You also need a personal Google Account: work, school and supervised accounts do not qualify, and you must be 18 or older.

For Memory summary specifically, Android Central and 9to5Google report that Google limits it to users in the US with an active Google AI plan, using it in English. Testers have seen it behave differently. Tom's Guide said it worked on a free plan in a browser, while Android Central could not get it to appear at all. If you do not see it yet, it may simply not have reached your account.
How to open Memory summary

paragraphs.title: 1. Use a browser first
paragraphs.text: Open gemini.google.com on a computer or in your phone's browser. Tom's Guide and 9to5Google both found it on the web, while reports on the Android and iPhone apps differ, so the web is the safest place to start.

paragraphs.title: 2. Go to Settings, then Personal Intelligence
paragraphs.text: Open Settings and choose Personal Intelligence. 9to5Google notes you can also go straight to gemini.google.com/personalization-settings.

paragraphs.title: 3. Open the Memory summary tab
paragraphs.text: Personal Intelligence has a Memory tab, where you switch memory on or off, and a Memory summary tab, where you read what Gemini has stored about you.
What you will find in it

The summary is split into sections instead of one long block. 9to5Google lists The Essentials (your core background, location and key relationships), Career and Professional Projects, Travel and Daily Gear, Media and Entertainment, and Fitness and Lifestyle. Each section is a short list of bullet points. Tom's Guide saw a similar split under Background, Relationships, Work, Interests and Preferences, so the labels may vary from account to account.
Read The Essentials section first. It is the short version of who Gemini thinks you are, and a wrong city, job or family detail there will color answers in every new chat.
How to fix or delete what it knows

paragraphs.title: 4. Tell it what to change in plain words
paragraphs.text: At the bottom of the summary there is a text field. Type what should be added or removed, the way you would say it to a person. 9to5Google says Gemini may ask a follow-up question when the request is unclear.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: Remove an old detail
paragraphs.text: Remove that I work at [old company]. I now work at [new company] as a [role].

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Add context you want it to use
paragraphs.text: Add that I prefer short answers with bullet points, and that I am planning a trip to [city] in [month].

paragraphs.title: 5. Use the pencil icon for bigger edits
paragraphs.text: The pencil icon in the top right of the summary lets you make wider changes than a single line, according to 9to5Google.

paragraphs.title: 6. Check Memory history
paragraphs.text: The three dot menu has a Memory history option that shows when a piece of information was added or changed. It helps when you want to know which chat taught Gemini something.

paragraphs.title: 7. Delete everything, or stop it learning
paragraphs.text: Tom's Guide says you can delete the whole summary. To stop Gemini from collecting more, switch Memory off: on the web, open Menu, then Settings and help, then Personal Intelligence; in the mobile app, tap Menu, then your profile picture or initial, then Personal Intelligence.

Deleting a line in the summary is not the same as deleting the chat it came from. Google's help page says that to remove something Gemini knows, you delete every chat that contains it in Gemini Apps activity, and it can take a little time before Gemini stops using deleted chats.
Where memory does not apply

Google's help page says memory works in the Gemini mobile app, the Gemini web app, Gemini in Chrome where available, and Gemini on smartwatches. It is not used in Gems or in Live chats. If you connected other apps, Google says you need to delete the related chats and disconnect the app, and changes made inside a connected app, such as a deleted email, can take days to reach Gemini.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Check if an answer used your memory
paragraphs.text: Did you use anything from my past chats to write that answer? If yes, tell me which details.

Google's help page suggests asking exactly this kind of question, and it also says you can correct Gemini directly in a chat while Memory is on. The page is honest that Gemini might still get things wrong after a correction, so check the summary again after a fix.

The weak spot today is reach. Memory summary is limited by country, language and plan, the mobile apps lag behind the web, and the exact section names differ between reports. The useful habit is simple: open the summary once, delete what is wrong or too personal, and come back after any big change in your job, home or plans.
